RSRCC

Regional Change Comprehension

A benchmark for general image-input VLMs answering localized questions about before/after satellite imagery.

Roie Kazoom, Yotam Gigi, George Leifman,
Tomer Shekel, Genady Beryozkin · Google Research

2026 preprint · arXiv:2604.20623v1

The benchmark predicts answers. Its construction pipeline uses specialist segmentation, but evaluated chat models do not need that pipeline.

Specialist models construct the dataset

Segmentation produces candidate changes. An image–text encoder screens them. A retrieval-conditioned judge checks ambiguous regions before QA generation.

Original figure 2. These components curate examples; they are not mandatory inference tools for the tested chat models.

Original paper, figure 2 and section 3
RSRCC

Best-of-N resolves ambiguous construction candidates

  1. Predict temporal semantic maps and extract connected candidate regions.
  2. Compare cropped evidence with class prompts using a remote-sensing-adapted SigLIP encoder.
  3. Retrieve similar annotated examples for ambiguous candidates.
  4. Use Gemma-3-4B to score candidate interpretations and retain high-confidence hypotheses.
  5. Use Gemini-2.5-Flash to generate varied questions conditioned on the accepted region and label.

The language model participates in semantic validation as well as linguistic generation. The main text’s “vision-derived label” wording should be read alongside this judge stage.

A no-change answer does not segment unchanged land

QuestionExpected output
Did the described object or area change?A negative answer when the queried change is absent
Which of these descriptions fits the image pair?The stable-scene option when appropriate
Where are all unchanged pixels?A spatial mask, outside the main RSRCC answer task

A pair may contain several changes while a question refers to one region or category. The human-verification protocol explicitly asks reviewers to judge the queried change, not every visible difference.

Paper, section 4 and appendices F, O
RSRCC

Several counts need careful interpretation

  • The release has 126,131 QA records. Do not call them 126,131 independent image pairs.
  • Appendix I’s “test-only” class table totals 126,131, rather than the released test split’s 21,999 rows.
  • The appendix mentions 10,007 processed pairs but then reports 89,031 change rows and 37,100 no-change rows.
  • Appendix O describes three human evaluators; appendix P refers to four external annotators.

These are documentation inconsistencies in the inspected version. They do not by themselves prove invalid labels or data leakage. Reproduction needs a record-to-image mapping and an explicit annotation protocol.

Paper, appendices I, O, P; public split metadata
RSRCC

Construction can shape the test distribution

  • The pipeline selects candidates that its segmentation, encoder, and judge accept. Difficult rejected cases may be underrepresented.
  • Gemini Flash generates QA text; Gemini and Gemma also appear among evaluated model families.
  • Human checks support annotation quality, but do not alone establish independence from generator phrasing or selection bias.
  • The inspected documentation does not establish a geographic split audit or image-level leakage check across all QA records.

These are risks to investigate, not measured evidence of contamination. The paper itself acknowledges a predefined semantic inventory and uncertain generalization to novel or compositional changes.

Paper, question-answer extraction, section 5 and appendices O–P
RSRCC

The remaining distinction is spatial, relational evaluation

RSRCC establishesA different evaluation would test
General chat VLMs answering temporal image questionsGeneral chat VLMs returning query-specific regions
Localized semantic descriptionsExplicit source, destination, gain, loss, and within-class predicates
Answer and caption metricsForeground spatial accuracy with output-format controls
A curation-stage prompting comparisonDevelopment-selected prompting and held-out transfer for the answering pipeline

“General VLMs on change questions” is already occupied. A new benchmark needs evidence for the additional spatial or relational capability it measures.
